title: enumerate proper 2-colourings of the b-conflict graph (homophonic crib-split space)
hypothesis: the homophonic b-graph admits FAR FEWER crib-feasible colourings than the bijective 3-colouring space, narrowing the selector's crib-position freedom
best_partial: 512 structural 2-colourings (256 distinct chart-pairs) vs 23887872 bijective 3-colourings; narrows=True
insights: b-conflict graph: 10 edges over 24 crib nodes. Connected structure: 9 edge-bearing component(s) (sizes [2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2]) + 5 isolated nodes. A proper 2-colouring is a crib-feasible split of the 24 crib positions into 2 homophonic charts.

COUNT (exact, factored over components): the forced splits give 512 structural 2-colourings (256 up to chart-swap); 256 DISTINCT pinned chart-pairs. With the 5 isolated crib nodes free to sit in either chart, the full 2-colouring count is 16,384. The bijective full graph admits 23,887,872 proper 3-colourings.

HOMOPHONIC NARROWS THE CRIB SPACE: the homophonic model's forced crib-split space (512 structural 2-colourings) is SMALLER than the bijective 3-colouring space (23,887,872). The cribs pin the 2-chart partition far more tightly than the bijective view could see -- the structural opening 116 hinted at, made quantitative.

SCOPE: this counts crib-feasible CHART PARTITIONS, not decryptions -- the 73 free positions still need a selector value and the charts' free (non-crib) entries are open (092/093 under-determination). 118 does the exact forced/free entry accounting per partition; 119 the determinacy floor + decrypt census.
